newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Sept 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Sept 18.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Britain could return 40 million stg of Nazi gold, currently in the Bank of England, to Jewish groups. The British foreign secretary Malcolm Rifkind is currently in talks with his Swiss opposite number Flavio Cotti about what happened to an estimated 4.6 billion stg of looted gold which was deposited in Swiss banks.
OFGAS POISED TO STEP UP PRICE CUTS REGIME

The director of Ofgas Clare Spottiswoode will push for further reductions in British Gas's revenues if the company decides to take her plans for cuts in pipeline charges to the Monopolies and Mergers Commmission. Analysts estimate that further action by Ofgas could cost British Gas a further 150 million stg to 200 million stg annually.
The European Commission is to investigate Credit Lyonnais's repurchase of its former subsidiary, Societe de Banque Occidentale, for 50 million francs (6.2 million stg).
SHAKE-UP AT HOME TO BOOST SBC PROFITS

Swiss Bank Corporation today announced an overhaul of its domestic banking network which will emphasise the increasing importance of London and Chicago in its expansion. The bank will close 80 Swiss domestic branches with the loss of 1700 jobs over the next three years, and is to radically alter the way it provisions bad loans.
RED ALERT STAYS IN FORCE FOR INVESTORS IN RUSSIA

Worries about political risk, crime and the possible power vacuum in the event of Boris Yeltsin's death are contributing to Russia continuing to lose out to other emerging markets when it comes to attracting Western investment. A survey by Control Risks Group found that China was attracting 25 times more direct investment than Russia.
KIBBUTZ LONDON FLOAT BREAKS NEW GROUND

Plasson, an Israeli plastics firm set up in 1963, is to become the first kibbutz-created company to float on a stock market outside Israel. The company is planning for a full listing on the London Stock Exchange.
